extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners operating under the Korean Patent Act (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/legal standards for entitlement, inventorship, succession, document content, and special procedures for filing and examination under the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to a Patent (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who makes an invention or his/her successor is entitled to a patent under the Patent Act; however employees of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board are not entitled to a patent while in office except by inheritance or bequest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entitlement originates at the time the invention is completed and continues until final rejection or registration. Care must be taken (by examiners and applicants) to confirm applicant identity (e.g., via PatentNet) and to reject applications filed by KIPO employees while in office; special procedures apply where entitlement is transferred or the employee has retired/ transferred/ files within two years of retirement (outside search, multiple examiner consultation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Inventorship and Joint Applications (Article 33(2) & Article 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more persons jointly make an invention, they are jointly entitled to a patent and all entitled persons shall jointly file a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a patent on a jointly-made invention, all joint owners must participate in filing; failure of only some joint owners to file can be ground for rejection or invalidation. Joint ownership has partnership-like aspects: joint owners generally may not transfer their interest without consent of the other joint owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Inventor — Substantial Contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor is someone who creates technical ideas using the laws of nature and makes substantial contributions to the creation of those technical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of who should be treated as an inventor: (Ex1) who newly presents/adds/concretely conceives ideas to solve the technical problem; (Ex2) who embodies or reduces to practice novel ideas via experiments; (Ex3) who provides specific means and methods to achieve the purpose/effects; (Ex4) who contributes through concrete advice and guidance. Non-inventor examples: mere problem-providers, general managers, technicians who only follow directions or arrange data, or providers of funding/equipment who only support creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship in Joint Inventions — Meaningful Contribution & Mutual Complementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two persons create an invention, those who jointly made the invention are inventors; each inventor must have, even partly, made a meaningful contribution to completion through mutual complementation in the technical process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technically, joint owners must have cooperated in the completion of the invention. Patent will not be granted if only part of joint owners file the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and Addition of Inventor During Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may add or correct omitted/misspelled inventor names until an examiner determines the patentability of the claimed invention; after an examiner's determination, addition of a new inventor is generally not accepted except for corrections of errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment changing inventor name is submitted during examination, the examiner need only determine if omission/misspelling was by mistake and need not request evidential documents unless there are 'special reasons' (e.g., suspected intentional omission to address a ground of rejection). Where examiner reasonably suspects the listed inventor is not genuine (e.g., inventor not natural person, a minor not capable of creating the invention), the examiner may order amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divulgence and Misappropriation of Confidential Information (public-official restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information on an invention in a patent application acquired in the course of work is protected; divulgence (intentional or accidental) to a third party and misappropriation (working the invention or filing related patent/utility model against right holder's intention) are offenses. Certain public officials and employees of specified institutions can be subject to criminal liability for divulging confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential information includes items required to be kept secret under the Patent Act and related acts and items with considerable benefits when kept secret. Public-official-status is interpreted to include employees of public corporations equivalent to administrative institutions after individual consideration; Article 226(2) recognizes executives/employees of special digitizing institutions as employees of KIPO for purposes of liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Legitimate Right-Holder Against Applications Filed by Unentitled Persons (Articles 34 & 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application filed by an unentitled person is rejected or a patent granted to an unentitled person is invalidated for lack of entitlement, a subsequent application filed by the legitimate right-holder may be deemed filed on the date of the unentitled person's filing (retroactive effect), subject to specific conditions and time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key conditions: (1) The legitimate-holder's subsequent application is deemed filed on the date of the initial unentitled filing provided it is filed within 30 days after the rejection becomes final (or within 30 days after an invalidation trial decision becomes final). (2) Patentability, term calculation and application of provisions for the legitimate-holder's application are determined from the initial filing date. (3) If a third party filed between the unentitled filing and the legitimate-holder's filing, the legitimate-holder's application with retroactive date prevails; the third party's application may be rejected. (4) If patent was wrongly granted to unentitled person, it can be invalidated via invalidation trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural Measures and Documents to Protect Legitimate Holder (filing requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke Articles 34/35 protection, the legitimate holder must file an application (Annexed Form No.14) to KIPO attached with specification, abstract or drawing(s), evidential document of legitimate holder of right, and evidential document of representation if a representative is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the legitimate holder wishes the subsequent application to receive the earlier filing date effect, they must include the specified application form and supporting documents when filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Requirement for Retroactivity of Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention disclosed in the description/drawings and the claimed invention of the legitimate-holder's application must be included within the scope of invention of the unentitled person's application for retroactive filing date to apply; if the legitimate-holder's application contains inventions outside the scope of the unentitled person's disclosure, retroactivity does not apply to those out-of-scope inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple inventions are included in the legitimate-holder's application but only some were disclosed in the unentitled person's application, the out-of-scope inventions will not benefit from the earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Examination Request for Applications by Legitimate Holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when the legitimate-holder's subsequent application is filed more than three years (five years for older filings before 2017-03-01) after the unentitled person's initial filing, a request for examination can be made within thirty days from the date the legitimate-holder filed the application (Article 59(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request for examination is filed on the same day as the legitimate-holder's application filing, the request is deemed effective; the 30-day window is to enable protection despite significant delay from the initial unentitled filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on Patent Term When Legitimate Holder Prevails
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is granted to a legitimate holder under Articles 34 or 35, the patent term shall be 20 years calculated from the day after the filing date of the application by the unentitled person (i.e., the initial application's filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term and other time-based effects are computed from the initial unentitled filing date when protection applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Patent Application Documents (Article 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must include a cover sheet stating applicant and agent information, title of invention, and inventor name(s); it must be accompanied by a specification containing description and claims, necessary drawings, and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet is the essential information sheet. The specification must include the description of the invention and the claims; drawings where necessary should be provided. The abstract is for technical information only and must not be used to define the scope of the invention (Article 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Cover Sheet Content and Title Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet must include: (1) name and domicile (or if corporation, name and place of business) of applicant; (2) name and domicile/place of business of agent (and patent firm info and designated attorney if applicable); (3) title of the invention; (4) name and domicile of inventor. The title should be brief and concise and identical to the title in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet also should indicate applicant code, priority claims, claims on grace-period disclosure exceptions, and request for examination. The title must reflect the subject matter and match the specification exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Succession to Entitlement (transfer before/after filing, notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: If entitlement to a patent is transferred before filing, no special succession proceeding is required, but where transfer occurs after filing, succession is effective only when a notice of change of applicant (Annexed Form 20) and supporting evidential documents are submitted before registration of the application (except universal succession).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required attachments include evidential documents stating grounds for change, permission/approval/agreement/consent from third party if necessary, and proof of representative's authority if proceedings are by representative. A single notice may be filed for multiple applications if contents are the same. For succession after death, documents proving death and inheritance (death certificate, family relation certificate, will, or representative consent) must be provided to resume interrupted proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Special Succession and Simultaneous Filings (conflicting applications/changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple applications or notices of change arise from the same entitlement (succeeded from same person) and are filed on different or same dates, special rules determine who may obtain a patent or which notice is effective: earlier filing prevails if different dates; if filed on same date, succession/notice effective only for a person mutually agreed upon by applicants; examiners shall set a consultation period and may reject applications if no agreement is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will designate a period (in the name of the Commissioner) for consultation and request results; if applicants fail to agree, succession may not be effective and applications may be rejected as filed by unentitled persons. Results of consultations must be submitted with evidential documents (signed/sealed) and may lead to measures such as withdrawal of some conflicting applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-pledgeability of Entitlement to Obtain a Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An entitlement to obtain a patent shall not be pledged; any pledge established upon the entitlement to obtain a patent is not effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once patent rights are registered, however, a pledge can be established on the registered patent right or utility model right. This distinction between pre-registration entitlement (not pledgeable) and registered rights (pledgeable) is emphasized.
